newsitem.title: USA: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.
newsitem.headline: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.

text.p: Boxed beef traded sharply higher on light demand and offerings. Once again, processors had to pay higher money for their live cattle needs and succeeded in forcing this additional cost onto retailers seeking to fill immediate featuring needs. Consequently, most all cuts traded higher this week leading to a dramatic increase in cutout values.

However, forward interest was very light as retailers balked at higher price levels and took a look at other protein sources. Loin primal displayed the biggest gains as tenderloins and top butts had huge increases.

Closely trimmed items also traded sharply higher on light demand. Continued light carcass weights, coupled with reduced slaughter levels, helped stimulate beef trimmings sharply higher on light to moderate demand and light offerings. Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items traded higher on light to moderate demand and light offerings with the fed cattle grinds experiencing the biggest gains.

For the week - Select and Choice rib primal 4.00 to 5.50 higher; Select and Choice chuck primal 5.50 to 8.00 higher; Select and Choice round primal 5.50 to 8.00 higher; Select and Choice loin primal 7.00 to 9.00 higher; Closely trimmed items 6.50 higher; Beef trimmings 6.50 higher; Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items 2.00 to 6.00 higher.

The Estimated Composite of Boxed Beef Cutout values of Choice 1-3 550/700 carcasses Up 6.68 at 106.08; 700/850 Up 6.51 at 105.96; Select 1-3 550/700 carcasses Up 6.51 at 102.74; 700/850 Up 6.46 at 102.19.
COW AND BULL CARCASS, BONELESS PROCESSING BEEF, CUTTER COW CUTOUT

The boneless beef market was sharply higher this week on moderate to fairly good demand and light to moderate offerings. The reduced marketing of slaughter cows, especially in the southern region, resulted in the limited availability of boneless beef. Grinders had been buying primarily for immediate needs over recent weeks.
Demand, however, improved this week as many fast food grinders sought product to increase finished inventories, which was stimulated by the announcement of upcoming fast food hamburger promotions.

The cow carcasses also traded higher in response to the advances made in the boneless beef market. Moreover, the cow cuts market moved at higher price levels on light supplies and moderate to good demand, especially on the 100% lean items.
Utility carcasses 4.00-5.00 higher; Cutter mostly 3.00 higher; 90% boneless beef 7.00-9.50 higher; 85% 3.50-8.00 higher; 75% 3.00-4.50 higher; 65% 4.50-6.50 higher.
The Cutter cow carcass gross cut-out value for Thursday, February 27, 1997 was estimated at 78.48 per cwt., up 4.93 from a week ago Friday.
